## Summary

I implemented rejection of owners whose email domain is on a disposable-domain blocklist, returning **400 Bad Request**, following the existing owner-validation patterns in this Spring Boot app.

Changes:

1. **`rest/validation/DisposableEmailDomains.java`** (new) — a `@Component` holding the blocklist (`mailinator.com`, `tempmail.com`, `guerrillamail.com`) with an `isDisposable(email)` method that does a case-insensitive match on the domain after the final `@`. Null/blank/`@`-less values are treated as not disposable (syntactic validity is already enforced by Bean Validation's `@Email`).

2. **`rest/advice/DisposableEmailDomainException.java`** (new) — a `RuntimeException` mirroring the existing `InvalidOwnerPostcodeException` style, carrying the rejected email.

3. **`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — injected the new component and added a `rejectDisposableEmailDomain(...)` check in `addOwner`, placed alongside the other field-validation guards (after `rejectBlankOwnerFields`).

4. **`rest/advice/ExceptionControllerAdvice.java`** — added an `@ExceptionHandler` that renders the exception as a 400 `ProblemDetail` with an `errors: ["email"]` array, matching the shape of the other owner-creation error responses.

The acceptance test `errorRejectsDisposableDomain` (posting `x@mailinator.com`) now passes, and the full suite is green.
